entry.title: Edge No Bleed 1.0.0
entry.content:
Edge No Bleed

Eliminates the persistent 1-2px margin gap where desktop wallpaper bleeds through along screen edges behind maximized windows.

The Problem

On Windows 10 and 11, users running dark-mode themes, IDEs, terminals, and browsers frequently notice a razor-thin 1-2px strip of desktop wallpaper leaking through along the edges of maximized windows (especially at the bottom or side monitor borders).

Why This Happens

  • DWM Frame Padding & Fractional DPI Rounding: Windows calculates maximized client coordinates by converting logical device-independent units into physical screen pixels. At fractional display scaling factors (such as 125%, 150%, or 175%), rounding calculations frequently leave a 1-2 physical pixel deficit against the work area, exposing bright desktop wallpaper pixels.
  • Invisible Margin Bounds: Normal Win32 maximized frames hang invisible resize margins off-screen, but custom-chrome and modern applications (such as Chromium, Electron, and Windows Terminal) size their own frames and can fall short of physical display boundaries.

How It Works

Edge No Bleed runs as a dedicated tool mod within Windhawk without injecting invasive hooks into third-party processes. It monitors window position and state changes via out-of-context WinEvents on a dedicated message-loop worker thread:

  1. When a window is maximized, the mod measures its true visible frame bounds using DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS) against the monitor's work area (MONITORINFO::rcWork).
  2. If a 1-2px fractional rounding gap is detected, the mod expands the window frame via SetWindowPos by the exact measured discrepancy, sealing the edge flush against the screen.
  3. If an auto-hide taskbar is active on that edge, the mod detects it via SHAppBarMessage(ABM_GETAUTOHIDEBAREX) and preserves the 1px mouse-hover reveal strip.

Comparison With Other Mods

  • Maximized Window Margins: That mod intentionally adds large margins (10px to 200px, macOS-style) by shrinking the system work area with AppBars. Edge No Bleed does the opposite: it eliminates unwanted 1-2px fractional DPI gaps so maximized windows sit completely flush.
  • Classic Maximized Windows Fix: That mod is exclusively designed for the legacy Classic 3D Theme on Windows 10/11 using region clipping (SetWindowRgn). Edge No Bleed targets standard modern DWM themes and dark-mode setups.

entry.title: Start Menu Groups 1.0.0
entry.content:
Start Menu Groups

Add your own app groups to the Windows 11 Start menu, before or after the Pinned section (or in place of the built‑in All → View: Category grid), using the same look as Start: rounded tiles with an icon preview, an overflow cluster for the remaining apps and the group name underneath.

Designed for the Windows 11 Start menu (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe).

Features

  • Your own groups — create any number of groups and put any Start menu app in them, desktop and Store apps alike. An app can be in several groups.
  • Apps, programs and websites — each item is a Start app (picked by name or app ID), a program, file or folder (full path with optional arguments), or a website opened in the default browser.
  • Custom names and icons — every item can have its own label and icon: an .ico, .exe, .dll or image file, an image link (such as a website's favicon), a Fluent icon by its code (e.g. E774) or an emoji.
  • Native look — rounded tiles, borders and colors match Start's own category view and follow the Windows light / dark theme.
  • Resizable tiles — give each group its own tile size, from 1 × 1 up to 6 × 4 (24 apps). Bigger tiles take more cells of the group grid. A 1 × 1 tile is a single app on its own, without a group.
  • Overflow cluster — when a group has more apps than fit, the last cell shows the rest as small icons; click it to open the whole group.
  • Right‑click menu — right‑click an app in a group for Edit, Run as administrator, Open file location, Pin to taskbar, App settings and Uninstall, like Start's own apps.
  • Size presets — Default, Small and Large presets for the tiles, icons and names, plus control over gaps, corner radius, colors and group names.
  • Placement — show the groups before or after Pinned, after Recommended / Recent, or after the All section, with an optional section title.
  • Hide Start's sections — optionally hide Start's own Pinned, Recommended and All sections and use only your groups.
  • Settings window — right‑click the groups in Start → Customize Start Groups for a visual editor with drag & drop (see Settings window).
  • Import / export — all settings can be exported to and imported from a JSON file.

Screenshots

The settings window, with drag & drop editing of groups and apps:

Setting it up

Everything is configured on the mod's Settings tab in Windhawk, in sections:

  • Groups — add a group with Add new item, give it a name, a tile size and its items. For a Start app, enter the app's name exactly as it appears in Start (for example Calculator, Visual Studio Code; case doesn't matter), or its app ID (AUMID, such as Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App). For a program, its full path (a program, file or folder) and optional arguments; for a website, its address. Reorder groups with the arrows.
  • Behavior — where the groups appear, the section title, app names and tooltips, sorting, empty groups, the number of columns when a group is opened, and hiding Start's own sections.
  • Tiles, Icons, Group names — sizes, gaps and colors. The defaults match Start's own category view.

Changes apply to Start as soon as you click Save settings.

Settings window

Right‑click the groups in Start → Customize Start Groups (also added to Start's own right‑click menu, after Start settings) opens a settings window with the same settings, but easier to edit:

  • Groups — shows the groups the way Start does. Drag apps to reorder them or move them to another group, drag a tile to reorder the groups, drag a tile's corner to resize it, and drag apps from the All Apps list onto a tile to add them. The selected group and app are edited below the groups. Right‑click a tile to rename, duplicate or delete it.
  • Customization — the size preset (Default, Small, Large), gaps, corner radius, colors and group names.
  • Behavior — placement, section title, app names, tooltips, sorting and columns.
  • Built‑in sections — hide Start's own Pinned, Recommended and All sections.

Start apps are picked by name with suggestions from the apps in Start; programs have a file picker. Groups and items can be duplicated, and an app can be added on its own, without a group. Import / Export at the bottom of the navigation pane save all settings to, or load them from, a JSON file.

The window is hosted by File Explorer — the mod also loads into explorer.exe for this, and does nothing else there — because the Start menu process can't host one. It edits the same settings as Windhawk. Windhawk keeps them in a protected registry key, so Save shows an administrator (UAC) prompt for Windows PowerShell, which imports the new settings, and Start updates right after. The import checks that the settings file is exactly the one the window wrote, so no other program can change what gets saved. If the settings were changed in Windhawk while the window was open, Save asks before replacing them. The portable version of Windhawk isn't supported by the window.

Tile size and apps in the tile

Each group has two size settings:

  • Tile size — width × height of the tile, in app spots. 2 × 2 is the size of one of Start's own tiles; 1 × 1 is an app on its own, without a group.
  • Apps in the tile — apps per row × rows of apps, at most the tile size. Default fills the tile with one app per spot; the rest go in the overflow cluster.

A group can also hide its app names, its group name, or its tile background (no background, border or padding — just the apps, e.g. for a single app on its own).

Colors

Colors are #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB. Leave a color empty to follow the Windows theme and match Start.

Network access

The mod doesn't connect to the internet by itself, and the default settings don't contact any server: the default websites show a globe icon.

An icon set to an image link (http:// or https://, such as a website's favicon) is downloaded from that address by Windows' XAML image loader: a normal web request for the image, which sends your IP address and a user agent to that server. It happens when Start builds the tiles (when the mod loads, on a theme or settings change, and when a group is opened), and when the settings window shows the item. To avoid it, leave the icon empty or use a local file, a Fluent icon code or an emoji.

Compatibility

The mod reaches Start's UI directly, without XAML diagnostics, so it works alongside mods and tools that use them, such as Windows 11 Start Menu Styler.

Language

The groups are placed next to Start's pinned list, found by its element name, so they show in any display language. Two things go by Start's English titles: hiding Start's sections (Pinned, Recommended / Recent, All), and adding Customize Start Groups after Start settings in Start's own right‑click menu. In other languages, open the settings window by right‑clicking the groups instead.

Default configuration

Out of the box the mod adds these groups before the Pinned section, under an Apps heading:

  • Group 1 — Microsoft Store, Settings, Notepad, Weather
  • Group 2 — Camera, Paint, Calculator, Calendar
  • Favorites — Photos, Terminal, Notepad, Get Help (group name hidden)
  • Group 3 (3 × 3) — Sound Recorder, Voice access, Task Manager, Movies & TV, File Explorer, Sticky Notes
  • System (3 × 1) — Control Panel, Services, Run (group name hidden)
  • Websites (3 × 2) — YouTube, ChatGPT, Example, Google, Reddit, dan13.me

Empty groups are hidden. None of Start's own sections are hidden by default. Everything is configurable in the mod settings.

entry.title: Mac OS 27 Finder Bar 1.1.1
entry.content:
• Stacked notifications: in the floating layout, notifications from three apps or more are stacked, with the newest in front. The stack follows the theme, and the front card hides the cards behind it, which show only at the bottom edge.
  • The mouse wheel turns the stack to the next notification.
  • Dragging the front card aside dismisses it and shows the next one.
  • A click spreads the cards into the list with a spring animation; "Show less" stacks them again.
  • Scrolling the notification list, with the wheel or by dragging, is smooth. Cards pile up at the top and bottom edges instead of being cut off, as on Android.
  • The bell turns red when a notification arrives, like the microphone and camera icons. This replaces the red dot.
  • Notifications and notice pills are now separate switches. "Receive app notifications" (formerly "Windows notifications") is in the Notifications button group, and with the pills off, notifications still go to the bell. "Only the bar shows notifications" needs the pills, so it shows only when both are on.
  • Selection gradient: an optional second selection color blends the bar's selection pill and the menus' selection from one color to the other.
  • New "Test notifications" button in Menu Bar Settings. Each click sends a test notification from a different app.
  • Fix: the notifications panel now catches the mouse wheel and clicks over very clear glass. Before, they went to the window below.
  • README: demo of the stacked notifications.
  • "Clear" in the notifications panel slides the cards out one after another before removing them.
  • The bar slides up and down when it hides and shows (with the handle and with "Hide when a window is maximized").
  • With "Hide when a window is maximized", pointing at the top edge shows the bar over the window until the pointer leaves, as on macOS.
  • Settings backup: export the Menu Bar Settings to a file and import them again.
  • Num Lock and Scroll Lock pills, like Caps Lock.
  • Restart, Shut Down and Sign Out ask in a glass dialog.
  • Fix: the notice pill set to follow the bar had no glass with the Glass background and "live".
  • Fix: with the handle on, leaving full screen no longer shows the bar.
  • Fix: after the active app is minimized or closed, the bar goes back to "Finder".
  • Fix: moving between the bar's menus no longer flickers the app's window.
  • Fix: a full-screen video on another display now hides that display's bar.
  • Fix: optional updates (drivers, previews) are no longer counted as pending.
  • Fix: Windows' own volume, network and power icons no longer show in the bar's tray.
  • Fix: video thumbnails (YouTube) are cropped instead of stretched.
  • Fix: connected Bluetooth LE devices (mice, keyboards) now show in the Bluetooth menu and pill.
  • Fix: clicking the bell or Now Playing on another display while the panel is open.
  • Fix: "System Settings" is now "Ajustes do Sistema" in Portuguese.
  • Now Playing: the cover is enlarged once in high quality, and video thumbnails show whole over a blurred copy of themselves instead of a cropped, stretched middle.
  • The bar slides in more smoothly with the handle; windows move down once it's in place.
  • Fix: resting the pointer on a bar button could hide the bar or make it reload over and over on setups with displays at different scales.
  • Settings backup: the import replaces all the bar's settings, and the copy now includes "This window"'s look and the weather widget's glass.

entry.title: Windows Border Switch 1.2.6
entry.content:
• Fix taskbar, Quick Settings, and media control borders that could stay visible after a symbol lookup failure.
  • Discover borders through XAML islands and keep border updates running while symbols load.
  • Prevent XAML hook registration during unload and skip scans triggered by regular File Explorer windows.

entry.title: Explorer Item Pins 1.1.7
entry.content:
• Reduce repeated folder scans and unnecessary refreshes for missing pins, and recover a renamed pin on the first refresh when its previously resolved name disappears.
  • Rename the commands to Pin to top and Unpin from top.
  • Group display settings. After updating from 1.1.5, display settings are reset to their defaults. Check them again if you had changed any.

entry.title: SnapSentry 0.24.0
entry.content:
• Optional small picture of the screenshot in the notification
  • Optional line showing the folder the screenshot was saved in
  • Choose what clicking the notification does: copy, open the screenshot, open its folder, or keep it without copying. A click never deletes

entry.content:

entry.title: Round Everything Interface 2.1.0
entry.content:
• Hide the frame without a maximized window (new General option, off by default): each monitor shows its frame only while a window is maximized on it. Otherwise the frame and its shadow are off, and they come back together with the taskbar's look. The monitor corners and the bezel line stay up, and the work area stays reserved either way.
  • Transparent taskbar when nothing is maximized (new General option, on by default): with the option above on, the taskbar's own background and border line are hidden while no frame shows, so the wallpaper shows through. Off, the taskbar looks as it does without the mod.
  • Aero Peek with the hide option on: the peeked window decides. If it's maximized (or minimized from maximized) on a monitor, that monitor keeps its frame; every other monitor shows the taskbar's resting look.
  • Task View: the frame stays in place under Task View, so nothing has to come back when it closes and it no longer flickers on open or close. The taskbar keeps its look over Task View without its monitor corners; with "Hide the frame without a maximized window" on and "Transparent taskbar when nothing is maximized" off, every taskbar takes its native look there.
  • When the frame comes back, it has the maximized window's title-bar color right away.
  • Explorer's own windows have their titles read without being sent a message.
  • Fixed: taskbar thumbnails opened by a click (a grouped button, or "thumbnails on click" in Disable Taskbar Thumbnails) were taken for Task View and hid the frame on every monitor.
  • Fixed: after Windows updates that rearrange the taskbar's layout (e.g. KB5137006), the taskbar could blink every 1.5 seconds. The corner ears now find their place in the new layout; where there's none, the corners stay square instead.
  • Fixed: a frame waiting for its taskbar to reveal it could be withdrawn before it showed, briefly leaving the taskbar without its frame after a layout change.
  • Fixed: a monitor with no maximized window could keep the mod ticking at 60 Hz.

entry.title: Siri Plus Launchpad 1.3.0
entry.content:
• Themes reorganized: Glass (clear glass, as in the Mac OS 27 Finder Bar), Liquid glass and Custom glass, plus Light, Siri, Dark and OLED. Each theme keeps its own customization right under it in Appearance, the panel only shows what applies to the chosen theme and mode, and Restore theme defaults brings a theme back to how the mod comes.
  • Glass buttons: buttons, tabs, shortcut keys, menu icons and the settings controls drawn as clear, polished glass (can be turned off).
  • Animated backlight (off by default): a colored glow around the bar, the results box, the menus and the buttons, with 1 to 5 colors turning around them and an intensity setting.
  • Chrome details: an animated chrome border around the bar, the box and the menus (on by default only on OLED) and a chrome ring on the settings button under the mouse. They work on every theme: graphite on light surfaces, and still in Fullscreen. Both can be turned off.
  • Every selection in every theme: Glass, Colored, Frosted color and Two colors blended, with their colors, for the menus and the search results (the result under the mouse and the one Enter opens), instead of a dim veil.
  • OLED starts deep black: no glass effect and no backlight by default.
  • Text size of the results: 80 to 160 % (Apps and icons); rows grow with bigger text.
  • The settings window's own look: follow the theme, or a light or dark glass of its own with its own blur and transparency (Backup and defaults).
  • macOS-style alerts: backup and restore messages and confirmations (also "already exists, replace it?") are drawn inside the launcher, in the settings window's look, instead of Windows message boxes.
  • Floating mode:
    • The results box can open on mouse over.
    • Files and Clipboard stay open with nothing typed: recent searches, copied items, or a line saying there are none yet.
    • Applications gets the app tabs (All, the categories and your own tabs) in a row under the categories, and the first row of recent or most used apps, as in Original Siri.
    • Several selected apps can be put in a tab, added to a tab or removed from it at once.
  • Search ignores accents (on by default, can be turned off): "acao" also finds "ação" and the other way around, in apps, files, actions and the other categories.
  • Phone category (Phone Link), off by default, in its own settings section:
    • The linked phone (battery and connection) and its notifications as they arrive.
    • Shortcuts to Messages, Calls, Photos and Send files.
    • Notifications can be cleared one by one or all at once, and they scroll inside the box when there are more than it shows (1 to 10).
    • Ctrl+5 opens it in Original Siri.
    • Everything is read on this PC only; nothing in Phone Link is changed.
  • Fixed: Glass and Liquid glass no longer look smudged; they blur the background themselves in every mode.
  • Fixed: lowering the glass transparency no longer turns the glass smoky.
  • Fixed: Light performance mode no longer looks yellowish over light wallpapers.
  • Fixed: the Glass effect option now works on Dark and OLED.
  • Fixed: Liquid glass now bends all four edges.
  • Fixed: in lists with a remove button (Clipboard, Phone), the hover highlight no longer covers the button or the scroll bar.
  • Fixed: the Phone tab was missing in Floating and Window modes.
  • Fixed: the "Recent searches" title was cut off in translated languages.
  • Fixed: folders and tabs could be lost on PCs with very many apps in portable Windhawk.
  • Fixed: a Ctrl+click on empty space could crash Explorer.

entry.title: Adobe Dark Menus 1.2.0
entry.content:
• The Effect submenu of the After Effects right-click menu now opens as one dark column that scrolls, like the Effect menu on the menu bar.
  • Added a Scroll Long Menus with the Mouse Wheel setting, on by default: the mouse wheel now scrolls a menu taller than the screen.
  • Added a Darken Photoshop Message Boxes setting, on by default: Photoshop's message boxes, such as the prompt to save changes, are now dark.
  • Title Bar Color and Title Bar Text Color now say they need Windows 11, and sit right after Border Color in the settings.

entry.title: MacOS Style Dock 1.2.0
entry.content:
• New: Liquid Glass (off by default). The dock's rim bends what's behind it like real glass, instead of only a frosted blur. Turn it on by picking Lens, Reflection or Stretch in "Edge Style", and adjust "Edge Depth", "Edge Strength" and its own "Liquid Glass Blur".
  • Liquid Glass has two downsides: it trails the screen behind the dock by a frame or two, and while it's on, the taskbar is hidden from screenshots, screen recordings and screen sharing. If either is a problem, set "Edge Style" to Off for the plain frosted glass.
  • New shortcuts while Liquid Glass is on: Win+Ctrl+Shift+G freezes the glass so the taskbar shows up in screen captures, and Win+Ctrl+Shift+K turns Liquid Glass off at once in an emergency, until the mod's settings are saved again.
  • New: the system tray gets a background. By default it matches the dock (its glass, Liquid Glass, border and glow) as a smaller pill. Turn off "Match Dock Style" to give it its own color, opacity, blur and border. "Tray Padding" sets the room around its icons and clock.
  • New: per-pixel brightness limits behind the dock and the tray, on by default at 80, so bright windows behind them are dimmed and the tray's clock and icons stay readable. Under dark text it becomes a minimum brightness instead.
  • The tray's text and icon shadow can now be adjusted: color, opacity, blur and offset.
  • The tray now slides in and out of its hot corner without fading.
  • New dock options: "No Background", a Custom border (color, width and opacity), and None for "App Activity Indicators".
  • New dividers: one before the Recycle Bin (on by default), and up to 5 more at positions of your choice with "Custom Index Dividers".
  • New "Keep Icons Still" option, which turns off the bounce Windows gives icons as apps open, close, minimize or are restored.
  • Start can now stay in the dock: turn off "Hide Windows Start Button" to keep it at the front, with Windows' icon or your own ("Start Menu Icon").
  • "Squircle Color" has new options: Always Light, Prefer Light, Prefer Dark and Always Dark.
  • Custom icons now accept Mac .icns files as well as PNG and other images, at any size. Each icon now has a single "Margins" setting (-50 to 50) instead of a margin and a size.
  • Squircle icons: fixed icons showing another app's icon and icons that never got their tile. As a last resort, a tile is now made from the app's icon as Start shows it.
  • Fixed the dock and hot corners staying blocked after an exclusive full screen game was minimized or switched away from.
  • Settings are reorganized into new groups (Dock Size, Dock Color, Liquid Glass, Tray Color, Dock Items, Custom Icons, Hot Corners, Additional Settings). Settings saved in 1.1.2 don't carry over, so the mod starts from its defaults once. This is intended.
  • New defaults: "Magnification" 60 (was 70), "Dock Glow Spread" 8 (was 6), "Dock Glow Opacity" 63 (was 60).
  • The readme has a new Liquid Glass section near the top, links to macOS icon resources, and a new section on the system tray.

entry.title: Windows Key to Search 1.2
entry.content:
• Search now opens without simulating Win+S, so Win+S remaps (e.g. PowerToys Keyboard Manager) no longer interfere. Thanks to Asteski.
  • Other tools that use the Windows key, such as PowerToys remaps and AltSnap Win+drag, now work alongside the mod.
  • Releasing Win after a Win+click, drag, or scroll no longer opens Search.

entry.title: Quick Look 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Glass effects are supported. With ExplorerBlurMica, DWMBlurGlass or similar, the panel follows the effect like the rest of the window, in dark and in light mode. Its text is drawn solid instead of being added to the blur, and an image preview is never tinted by what is behind Explorer. Without an effect the panel is drawn exactly as before.
  • Zoom and pan for images. Double click an image to switch between fit and 100%, drag a zoomed image to pan it, and use the wheel (Shift for sideways) to scroll it.
  • Colors follow the Windows app mode. The text color now depends only on whether Windows is light or dark, so it no longer turns gray or white from one preview to the next. The background stays Explorer's own surface. The accent still comes from Windows.
  • Archives show the shell's own view without a name filter. A results folder cannot resolve the name of an item inside an archive, so the filter box is hidden there. Folders keep the filter.
  • Typing in the filter no longer opens an Explorer window. The panel's own results view is no longer treated as a navigation, and a navigation outside the previewed folder is cancelled silently.
  • The filter shows the right items. Only the matching direct children of the previewed folder are listed, with no duplicates and no stray file.
  • The icon in the properties view is taken from a frame the shell did not pad, so it fills its box instead of sitting tiny in the corner.
  • A folder inside an archive shows an empty date instead of the 1601 epoch.
  • Opaque images scale sharply. Only an image with real transparency is blended; a photo or a screenshot is scaled with a crisp filter.

entry.title: Text Capitalization 0.3.1
entry.content:
Text Capitalization

Select text and press Ctrl+Alt+P to capture the selection and open a compact picker. The selected text is shown in a read-only preview; Up/Down changes the highlighted case and updates the preview. Enter or clicking a case replaces the original selection with the transformed text. Escape cancels.

Default shortcuts are Ctrl+Alt+P (open picker), Ctrl+Alt+C (apply saved case immediately), Up/Down (navigate), Enter (apply highlighted case), and Escape (cancel). Shortcuts are configurable in Windhawk settings. On older Windhawk versions enter numeric VK values such as ctrl+alt+80 for Ctrl+Alt+P.

The picker never takes keyboard focus from the original editor. Selection capture and replacement use a guarded clipboard copy/paste workflow instead of depending on UI Automation selection detection. The clipboard is snapshotted and restoration is best-effort. The mode is remembered in Windhawk local storage.

Compatibility depends on the target app supporting copy and paste and leaving the original selection intact while the non-activating picker is shown. Elevated apps may reject simulated input if Windhawk/Explorer runs at a lower integrity level.

entry.title: Explorer Default Folder 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Default Folder

Opens every new File Explorer window or tab in a folder of your choice when it would otherwise open This PC, Home or Quick access.

Enter a folder in the mod settings, for example D:\Documents, %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, ~\Downloads, Downloads or shell:Downloads. Environment variables are expanded, and ~ or a relative path starts at your user folder. Leave the setting empty to keep Explorer's normal behavior.

You can apply the folder to new windows only, new tabs only, or both, and optionally reopen the folder you closed most recently instead.

Windows and tabs opened for any other folder are not changed, and navigating to This PC or Home yourself in an existing tab is not redirected. A new window or tab that is explicitly opened at This PC or Home (for example with the This PC desktop icon) can't be told apart from a default one, so it is redirected too.

How it works

The mod listens to Shell window events instead of polling, so it costs nothing while idle and redirects a new tab as soon as its first location loads. Its background thread never holds up Explorer's windows, even when the folder is on a slow or offline network share.

Compatibility

Designed for File Explorer on Windows 10 and 11. It uses documented Shell COM interfaces rather than version-specific Explorer symbols, so it does not need an update for each Explorer build.

entry.title: WinKlok 1.3.0
entry.content:
New features :

  • Repeating local events support (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly)
  • Optional seconds clock in calendar tab
  • Do Not Disturb toggle in notification panel & Notification count badge
  • Quick +1 min / +5 min buttons on finished timer popups
  • Search in notes bar & Markdown (.md) export in notes
  • Full WinKlok backup and restore option (.wkbak file)
  • Keyboard shortcuts for Stopwatch (Space and L)

Bug fixes & Improvements :

  • Smoother notification panel animations and scrolling
  • Improved event editor scrolling and repeat icons
  • More reliable Google Calendar syncing and auth handling
  • Better iCalendar (.ics) and Takeout archive imports/exports
  • Multi-monitor taskbar and UI rendering fixes
  • Improved notification snapshot privacy and cleanup
  • Improved Calendar tab UI
